Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap + competitive bake-off next steps (Omniva)
message_1_body:
Hi Claire and Samir,

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the deep dive. Below is a concise recap from our call and suggested next steps for the competitive bake-off. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you shared:
- Search/result relevance for customer support articles is inconsistent, leading to longer handle times and poor CSAT.
- Per-user cost for embeddings + retrieval is a concern given high daily query volume.
- Need predictable latency for live chat use case (95th percentile < 300ms desired).

Goals we heard:
1) Improve search relevance and reduce average handle time by ~20% within 6 weeks.
2) Control per-query cost under $0.02 equivalent.
3) Validate a production topology that meets latency SLOs in your EU region.

Decision criteria (as discussed):
- Relevance uplift measured on your labeled test set (primary)
- 95th percentile latency and tail behavior (secondary)
- Total cost per 1M queries (TCO)
- Ease of deployment / integration work (security and network constraints)

Vendor comparison notes from today:
- Redwood: strong batching/cache options, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private (we discussed a private VPC deployment if needed for compliance).
- Vendor X: good baseline relevance but concerns around steady-state cost and limited KV cache.
- Vendor Y: attractive price but missing streaming/structured output features you rely on.

Open questions for Omniva to confirm:
- Final size of labeled eval set you want used for the bake-off (we suggested 2k queries).
- Whether we should route the bake-off traffic via your EU VPC or use a hosted test to start.
- Any specific data retention/compliance constraints beyond standard SOC2 requirements.

Proposed bake-off plan (high level):
1) Alignment call w/ SEs to finalize test set and metrics (this week).
2) Redwood runs two back-to-back experiments vs. Vendor X and Vendor Y using your 2k eval set.
3) Shared vendor-comparison matrix with per-metric scores and cost modeling.
4) On-site or screen-share walkthrough of results and recommendation.

Next steps / asks from you:
- Confirm the eval set size and whether we can use the anonymized export you mentioned.
- Confirm preferred test topology (EU VPC vs. hosted).
- Tentative approve for a 2-week bake-off window starting Monday 5/31.

Attachments: I attached a short bake-off plan and a blank SOW template for procurement to review.

Happy to hop on a quick 15-min follow-up if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
Redwood Inference | High-performance LLM inference for production
